questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The sailors divided their (1)/ money around themselves and (2)/ the ship sailed on. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Ans: 2

Sol: Around means in all directions while among means surrounded by. The money was divided **among** the sailors, not around them. The correct sentence is: ‘The sailors divided their money among themselves and the ship sailed on.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Thank you for (1)/ getting me (2)/ of the hook. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Ans: 3

Sol: The phrase ‘get off the hook’ means to let someone escape from a difficult situation. It uses the word **‘off’**, instead of ‘of’. The correct sentence is: ‘Thank you for getting me off the hook.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Whine
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. Gripe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Whine"** means to complain in a feeble or petulant way. (किरकिराना/शिकायत करना)

 
 
• **Example: **She tends to whine about minor inconveniences.
 
 
 
• **Gripe **means to complain about something in a persistent, nagging manner. (शिकायत करना)
 
 
• **Example: **He often gripes about the long hours at work.
 
 
 
• Hence, to whine and to gripe both refer to complaining, making them similar in meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. Gripe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Gratification **(संतोष): Pleasure or satisfaction gained from something.

 
 
• **Example: **She felt immense gratification after completing the project successfully.
 
 
 
• **Luxury **(विलासिता): A state of great comfort or elegance, especially when involving great expense.
 
 
• **Example: **They enjoyed the luxury of staying in a five-star hotel.
 
 
 
• **Thrill **(रोमांच): A sudden feeling of excitement and pleasure.
 
 
• **Example:** The thrill of the roller coaster ride was electrifying.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Requisite
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. Precondition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Requisite"** means something that is necessary or required for a particular purpose. (आवश्यक)

 
 
• **Example:** Having a passport is a requisite for international travel.
 
 
 
• **"Precondition"** refers to a condition that must be fulfilled before other things can happen or be done. (पूर्वशर्त)
 
 
• **Example:** Passing the entrance exam is a precondition for being admitted to the university.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the word similar in meaning to **'Requisite'** is **'Precondition'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4 i.e. Precondition**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Peripheral** (परिधीय): Relating to or situated on the edge or periphery of something.

 
 
• **Example:** The company's peripheral activities are being outsourced.
 
 
 
• **Deadwood** (बेकार लोग या चीजें): People or things that are no longer useful or productive.
 
 
• **Example:** The manager decided to cut the deadwood from the team.
 
 
 
• **Trivial** (तुच्छ): Of little value or importance.
 
 
• **Example:** She often spends her time on trivial matters.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Dominate
questions.solution:
Ans: Surrender

Sol: Dominate means to have a commanding position. On the other hand, surrender means to stop resisting and submit to authority. Thus, the two words have opposite meanings. Prevail means to prove superior, dictate means state authoritatively and command means to give an authoritative order.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Squander
questions.solution:
Ans: Hoard

Sol: Squander means to waste resources like money or time in a reckless and foolish manner. On the other hand, hoard means to accumulate resources and hide or store away for later use. Thus, the two words have opposite meanings. Frivol means to behave carefree and superficial, dissipate means to disappear and expend means to spend or use up something.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

I would love to come to your party! Thank you for **(invites**) me.
questions.solution:
Ans: inviting

Sol: Inviting is an adjective which means the offer of something at a future date. The sentence talks about a party that is yet to occur. Hence, the present participle of ‘invite’ must be used. The correct sentence is: ‘I would love to come to your party! Thank you for inviting me.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

It must **(being)** quite an exciting time to be alive.
questions.solution:
Ans: have been

Sol: The modal ‘must’ is generally used as the perfect tense with the past participle of the main verb. In this case, the past participle of the main verb ‘be’ is ‘been’. The correct sentence is: ‘It must have been quite an exciting time to be alive.’

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

We drank a little and flung

X -soon were all asleep

Y -sand, thoroughly tired out, and

Z -ourselves down on the
questions.solution:
Ans: ZYX

Sol: Z is the first sentence as it continues the ‘flung’ part with ‘ourselves down’. Y comes next as it continues the ‘down on the’ part with the ‘sand’. Hence, ZYX is the correct combination of sentences, which is seen only in Option 4, making it the right choice.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Aqueous rocks of equal

X -exhibit in like manner a stratification nearly undisturbed

Y -over the lake-district of North America, and

Z -antiquity extend for hundreds of miles
questions.solution:
Ans: ZYX

Sol: Z comes first as it continues the ‘undisturbed’ part with ‘antiquity’. Y comes next as it continues the ‘hundreds of miles’ part with ‘over the lake-district’, as both signify places. Thus, ZYX is the correct combination of sentences which is seen only in Option 1, making it the right choice.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

The class is required to watch a video tutorial every day.

options.text: A video tutorial is required to be watched by the class everyday.
A video tutorial is watched by the class every day.
Every day the class watches a required video tutorial.
Every day the class is watching a required video tutorial.

questions.solution:
Ans: A video tutorial is required to be watched by the class every day.

Sol: Sentence 2 changes the meaning as it removes the ‘is required’ aspect, Sentence 3 also changes the meaning as it implies that the required video tutorial is indeed watched every day, which is not what the original sentence suggests and Sentence 4 uses the continuous tense which is grammatically incorrect. Only Sentence 1 keeps the meaning intact along with the tense and is the correct option.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. **

My father says, "Prices are shooting up alarmingly."

options.text: My father says that prices shoot up alarmingly.
My father says that the price was shooting up alarmingly.
My father says that prices shot up alarmingly.
My father says that prices are shooting up alarmingly.

questions.solution: When the reporting verb in direct speech is present tense, we do not employ changes in the tense in indirect speech. Hence, solution is Option 4.
